Title: 521kg meth haul originated in Laos, not Malaysia, says NCID
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 521kg of methamphetamine seized from a private jet in Laos did not originate from Malaysia and is believed have been destined for the Philippines.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the chartered private jet had flown empty from Subang Airport to Luang Prabang, Laos, before the drugs were loaded onto the aircraft.
"The drugs seized were meant for the Manila, Philippines market and not Malaysia.

Title: 10 vehicles catch fire at Johor Baru shopping centre
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Ten vehicles caught fire at the underground car park of a shopping centre in Jalan Wong Ah Fook.
Videos showing thick black smoke emerging from the underground level were shared on social media.
Three women suffered breathing difficulties in the incident.
Operation commander Senior Fire Officer 1 Suffian Sulaiman said the women received initial treatment from firefighters before a 48-year-old woman was taken to hospital.
The women, aged 48, 35 and 57, included a Singaporean, he said in a statement today.
Suffian said firefighters received a call about the incident at 3.40pm, with a fire engine from Larkin Fire and Rescue Station arriving about six minutes later.
The operation involved personnel and fire engines from the Larkin, Tebrau and Kempas fire and rescue stations, as well as the Mount Austin Volunteer Fire Brigade, with a total of 40 personnel.
The fire involved vehicles on the second basement level of the shopping centre.
Eight vehicles were 80 to 90 per cent burnt, while the other two were 20 to 30 per cent burnt, Suffian said.
Firefighters used two streams, each 91m long, from the building's fire protection system and fire engine pumps.
An inspection found that the fire protection system and exhaust fans at the site were not functioning.
Firefighters also checked the area to ensure no other victims were trapped.
The firefighting and inspection operations were still ongoing.

Title: Oil's new problem is logistics, not supply
Article:
MIDDLE East crude exports recently climbed to their highest levels since the start of the Iran war as more Gulf producers resume transit through the Strait of Hormuz —despite the continued threat of Iranian attacks. Yet oil prices remain stubbornly elevated, suggesting logistical problems are proving as disruptive as outright supply losses.
Crude flows through the embattled waterway reached 14.2 million barrels per day on a seven-day average on Sept 26, nearly 80 per cent of pre-war levels. While volumes have declined since, they will likely be revised higher because ships often disable satellite tracking systems while traversing the strait and for several days thereafter.
Either way, the trend is clear: a lot more crude is getting through the strait. So why is Brent still trading above US$100 per barrel? In a word, logistics.
For decades, the global oil industry functioned as a finely tuned system designed to move enormous volumes of crude and fuels over long distances at the lowest possible cost. The conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe have fractured that model, as a combination of record-high tanker rates, soaring insurance costs and a severe shortage of refining capacity has created bottlenecks across the energy supply chain.
Those problems may take months, if not years, to unwind, leaving consumers facing persistently high energy bills—even if the crude supply squeeze continues to ease.
Iran's blockade of Hormuz following the onset of the war with the United States and Israel on Feb 28 rapidly reshaped global oil flows. Gulf producers diverted supplies through alternative routes, buyers sought barrels from more distant regions and governments released unprecedented volumes of oil from strategic reserves.
One of the biggest changes was that Saudi Arabia — previously the world's largest oil exporter — diverted its exports through its East-West pipeline, which delivers crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. At one point this year, four per cent of global oil supplies were via this route.
However, after the pipeline came under attack by Iranian-backed Iraqi militias in early last month, Saudi Arabia was forced to redirect exports back to the Gulf via Hormuz, which it discovered, could be more easily transited than previously thought.
Saudi exports through Hormuz averaged three million bpd last month, the highest level during the conflict, according to Kpler.
While Saudi Arabia's crude exports through Hormuz last month were still only around half of pre-war volumes, the kingdom's exports could quickly near pre-war levels as the East-West pipeline gradually returns to normal operations.
Ironically, then, the attack on the East-West pipeline, which was intended to cripple Riyadh, may have instead weakened Teheran's most powerful leverage—its purported control of the strait — by demonstrating that large volumes can still transit Hormuz and other major export hubs despite continued attacks.
Yet the recovery remains fragile.
But geopolitics is only part of the story.
Freight and insurance costs, once a relatively minor component of the delivered price of oil, have become major price drivers, partly due to the current shuttle system operating around the Gulf.
At the same time, buyers are increasingly sourcing crude from the Atlantic Basin and shipping it to Asia over longer routes, further tightening tanker supply.
The result has been a surge in key tanker rates to record highs. Freight costs that once accounted for around three per cent of the delivered price of a barrel now represent roughly 27 per cent.
These costs are unlikely to normalise until trade flows return to something resembling their prewar pattern.
The loss of refining capacity in the Middle East and Russia, where Ukrainian drone attacks have crippled dozens of plants, has compounded the problem, particularly for diesel.
The Group of Seven's decision last week to release diesel from strategic stocks will likely provide only temporary relief as it does nothing to restore lost refining capacity.
What's more, refiners are increasingly competing for the medium-sour crude grades that generate higher diesel yields. Those barrels are concentrated in the Middle East and Russia, precisely the regions where supply disruptions remain most severe.
The result is that oil prices are no longer primarily a function of supply, but of the industry's ability to transport and process crude —making it much more challenging to bring these prices down.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Magnitude 5.0 earthquake strikes waters off Sandakan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.0 on the Richter scale struck the waters off Sandakan at 9.11pm tonight.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement tonight, said the earthquake was detected at coordinates 4.9 degrees North and 118.7 degrees East, at a depth of 10 kilometres.
The epicentre was located about 48 kilometres east of Lahad Datu.
Strong tremors from the earthquake were also felt in parts of Sabah's east coast," it said.
MetMalaysia said it would continue to closely monitor the situation following the earthquake.
The department also urged members of the public who felt the tremors to complete an official survey at https://forms.gle/fMioquNhRNQGCbZVA to assist in collecting field information.

Title: NST Leader: MyEG, e-Jamin cases underscore need to safeguard public money
Article:
Lately, questions have been raised over how private firms entrusted with collecting public funds handle government money.
The concerns warrant a closer examination of the safeguards governing contractor arrangements, particularly when large sums are outside direct government control. Two recent cases —involving Zetrix AI Bhd and Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd —highlight starkly different concerns — ranging from delayed remittance of collected funds to placing public money into commercial interest-bearing accounts.
Zetrix AI, acting on behalf of the Road Transport Department, collected RM314 million in various fees but failed to remit the funds.
Meanwhile, Dapat Vista, the operator of court bail payment system e-Jamin, collected RM193.71 million in deposits as at 2024 without a formal contract with the government.
Neither case should be viewed in isolation. Findings by the auditor general and the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on weaknesses in government oversight point to vulnerabilities in the systems governing outsourced collection and management of public funds.
[[nid:1549260]]
The issue is not simply whether any individual contractor breached its obligations, but whether the government's checks-and-balances were robust enough to prevent these failures.
The issues highlighted deep-seated structural and administrative vulnerabilities. Still, it's too much of a coincidence and it should compel enforcement authorities to examine every ministry, department and agency dealing with external billing contractors.
The Auditor General's Report 2/2026 revealed that the government failed to recover RM68.81 million in advance payments across 24 projects.
Almost 87 per cent of the debt remained uncollected for over 10 years. What went wrong? These ministries failed to pursue legal claims against errant contractors, many of whom conveniently went bankrupt or were dissolved.
They were also slow in filing "proof of debt" claims, leaving the government as an unprotected and unsecured creditor.
How was this permitted? The issue stems from special administrative exemptions granted to departments — exemptions that inexplicably continued even after contractors failed to meet standard Treasury controls meant to prevent operational bottlenecks.
However, there is now a legal tool to stop these abuses: the Government Procurement Act 2025 which introduces personal liability and strict penalties for unauthorised interference in public fund management.
The catch: the Act is enforceable only in 2027 so as to give ministries and private contractors a grace period.
The PAC recommended that the judiciary develop a proprietary system to eliminate vendor dependency and ensure full data ownership.
This sound advice should be extended across all arms of government, especially agencies that sub-contract critical functions or the collection of public funds

Title: Anwar says Muslims must embrace AI without losing their values
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Muslims must master technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) without losing their values, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
"Do not, in craving change and new knowledge, abandon our principles of faith, morals and character and be sidelined from the mainstream as good Muslims," he said.
Anwar said mastering AI was a must for the ummah.
"Must we master it? My answer is that it is a must. An ummah that abandons AI as new knowledge will be left behind," he said.
He said Malaysia's understanding of AI need not be copied wholesale from other countries, particularly the West.
Anwar was speaking at the opening of the 66th International Al-Quran Recitation and Memorisation Assembly (MTHQA) at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Anwar said the discussion on AI could be viewed through a question posed to the Islamic world nearly a century ago.
In 1929, scholar Sheikh Muhammad Basiuni Imran from Sambas wrote to Cairo journal Al-Manar asking why Muslims were backward when they represented the true religion, while the West was advancing.
The question was passed to Lebanese thinker Amir Shakib Arslan, whose answer was published in 1930.
Anwar said Arslan replied that Muslims accepted the religion but did not live by it, while others practised traits it taught, such as discipline, order, governance and cleanliness, and reaped the benefits.
"If young people asked that question today, it would still be relevant," he said.
Anwar said a mighty ummah required faith, knowledge, morals, character-building, the spirit of struggle and the courage to bring change, grounded in returning to the study, understanding and practice of the Quran.
He said several well-known ulama who recently visited Malaysia had urged a return to "turath", the Islamic intellectual legacy of more than 1,400 years, and that it should not be set aside because of new figures who claimed to master all knowledge.
The 66th MTHQA, held from Oct 6 to 10, carries the theme "Madani Dihayati, Ummah Diberkati" and brings together 50 participants from 38 countries, comprising 25 in the recitation (tilawah) category and 25 in the memorisation (hafazan) category.
Malaysia is represented by Mohamad Cik Hasnul Taqiyuddin Cik Sazali and Nur Syakura Mohamad Musa in the tilawah category, and Muhammad Izzul Afnan Sazali and Dina Hadfina Mohd Umarul Hisyam in the hafazan category.

Title: 148 cartons of suspected untaxed cigarettes seized in Hilir Perak
Article:
TELUK INTAN: Police seized 148 cartons of cigarettes suspected of being untaxed during a raid on a house in Hilir Perak.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Chua Kok Lian said the operation was carried out yesterday following information and intelligence gathered by the Marine Intelligence Unit in Kampung Acheh, Sitiawan, under Op Taring Landai (Op Contraband).
"Checks at the premises found several boxes containing cigarettes of various brands suspected of not bearing valid Customs duty stamps," he said in a statement.
The seized items were taken to the Hilir Perak district police headquarters. The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967.
Chua said investigations were ongoing to identify the source of the cigarettes, those involved and the distribution network.
Those convicted can be fined at least 10 times the amount of customs duty or RM100,000, whichever is higher.
The maximum penalty is a fine of up to 20 times the amount of customs duty or RM500,000, whichever is higher, or imprisonment of between six months and five years, or both.
Chua urged the public not to become involved in possessing, storing, selling or distributing untaxed goods, or acting as intermediaries.
He said Hilir Perak police would continue operations, intelligence gathering and enforcement action to curb the smuggling and distribution of contraband in the district.

Title: [UPDATED] Haze: All schools in Batu Pahat closed tomorrow after API hits 203
Article:
BATU PAHAT: All schools in the district will be closed tomorrow after the area recorded a very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 8pm today.
Batu Pahat district officer Kamalludin Jamal said the decision was made after the API reading reached 203.
Kamalludin, who is also the chairman of the District Disaster Management Committee, said the authorities were monitoring air quality and API readings with relevant agencies to ensure the safety and health of residents, particularly students and school staff.
"In line with the National Haze Action Plan and Education Ministry guidelines, measures related to haze management in schools must be implemented based on API readings and directives from the education authorities.
"Based on information reported on Oct 6, the API reading in Batu Pahat was 203 at 8pm, which is at a very unhealthy level.
"As the API reading exceeds 200, schools, kindergartens and nurseries in Batu Pahat will be closed on Oct 7 (tomorrow)," he said in a statement.
Following the closure, Kamalludin said schools would implement home-based teaching and learning if instructed by the ministry, Johor Education Department or Batu Pahat District Education Office.
He said this was subject to prevailing directives and guidelines, adding that schools must inform parents or guardians through official school channels of the home-based teaching and learning arrangements.
"The Batu Pahat District Education Office, together with relevant agencies, will continue to monitor API readings from time to time.
"Any decision on the reopening of schools must be based on developments in air quality and official directives from the authorities," he said.

Title: Amir Hamzah: Govt decisions can change 3.4 million lives
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Government decisions affecting "only 10 per cent" of the population can change 3.4 million lives, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said.
His remarks came ahead of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's presentation of 2027 Budget on Friday.
Reflecting on his senatorship, he said policymakers must look beyond the numbers and consider the lasting consequences of their decisions.
"I'm a numbers man. But sometimes you kid yourself by saying it's only 10 per cent, but let's be real, 10 per cent of the Malaysian population is 3.4 million people.
"If we affect 3.4 million people, somebody's life out there is dramatically changed. With what you do, you need to really work through and think through that."
He said decisions should not be made on impulse or without considering their consequences.
"You cannot be taking decisions on an impulse. You can't be doing it without thinking through the processes," he said at the Khazanah Megatrends Forum at the Mandarin Oriental Kuala Lumpur here today.
Khazanah Nasional Bhd managing director Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong and Khazanah Research Institute chairman Dr Nungsari Ahmad Radhi were also present.
Amir Hamzah said government decisions had widespread and lasting effects, making it important to consider how they could change people's lives.
He said the Fiscal Responsibility Act provided safeguards for managing public finances.
"Bringing down fiscal deficits to below a certain level is important to make sure the fiscal position of the government is strong enough to ride and grow the country going forward.
"Because what we don't want to do is borrow from our children and our grandchildren," he said.
Amir Hamzah said wealth generated from depleting resources, including oil and gas, must also be preserved so future generations could benefit.
He said the funds could be used in areas including education, skills development and health.
He said the broader aim was to improve people's lives.
"Maybe not for us, maybe for our children, maybe for our grandchildren," he added.

Title: MCBA launches internal probe into Laos drug seizure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) has launched an internal investigation following the seizure of 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private jet reportedly arriving in Laos from Malaysia.
Its director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain however declined to elaborate on the aspects being probed.
He clarified that the investigation was limited to MCBA, while the drug seizure case fell under the jurisdiction of the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department.
"We are conducting an internal investigation on our side, but further developments on the case should be referred to NCID as it involves drugs," he said when contacted.
Earlier today, media reports said Lao police had seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a
private jet reportedly arriving from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport
, with 13 people detained in connection with the case.
The Vientiane Times, citing the Lao Security Newspaper, reported that a security operation was conducted on Oct 1 following information received by provincial police on Sept 21 about a drug trafficking syndicate believed to be planning to smuggle narcotics across the border by air using a private aircraft.

Title: Johor wants jobs that make workers think twice about Singapore: Exco
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) is targeting higher-value careers that can persuade Johoreans to work locally instead of crossing the Causeway for better pay, said Lee Ting Han.
State investment, trade and consumer affairs committee chairman said the objective was not to match Singapore salaries ringgit-for-ringgit, but to improve the overall economics of working in Johor through better pay, career progression and quality of life.
"The JS-SEZ is not about matching Singapore salaries ringgit-for-dollar. Because of the exchange rate, that may not be realistic or the right benchmark.
"Our objective is to change the economics of working in Johor - to offer good salaries, meaningful career progression and quality of life, without Johoreans having to spend hours every day crossing the Causeway.
"The initial JS-SEZ target is 20,000 skilled jobs by 2034, but that should be the starting point, not the finishing line.
"The real transformation happens when major investments create an entire ecosystem of higher-value jobs - from engineers and technicians to digital, financial and professional services and lift local SMEs into global supply chains.
"The key performance indicator cannot just be billions of ringgits invested; it must be how many Johoreans we move from RM3,000 jobs to RM5,000, from RM5,000 to RM8,000, and eventually into RM10,000-and-above careers.
"Ultimately, we want to reach a point where a young Johorean receives two job offers - one in Singapore and one in Johor and the Johor offer is good enough that he or she genuinely has to think twice.
"We may not compete with Singapore on currency, but we can compete on the total proposition: salary, career, cost of living, family and quality of life.
"When that choice happens at scale, then we can say the JS-SEZ has truly succeeded.
"We are already beginning to see this. EcoCeres in Tanjung Langsat has created more than 300 quality jobs, including 185 held by Johoreans, with reported salaries ranging from RM3,000 to RM15,000 depending on skills and technical expertise.
"And this is not limited to one company. We are attracting companies such as Wiwynn in AI-server and computing hardware, while Brooks Automation is building advanced semiconductor automation capabilities in Johor, with positions ranging from engineering specialists and senior manufacturing engineers to manufacturing management.
"The data-centre ecosystem is another example: current Johor vacancies include data-centre engineering roles around RM5,000-RM7,000 per month, while the market also has specialised technical positions reaching higher levels.
"These are the kinds of jobs we want to multiply - not simply more jobs, but better jobs with stronger career pathways for Johoreans," he told Business Times,
Lee said the focus was therefore on building an industrial and services ecosystem capable of raising household incomes and retaining skilled workers in Johor.
The strategy comes as the debate over wage arbitrage - Johoreans earning Singapore dollars while living in Johor - increasingly highlights the gap between the two labour markets and the challenge of creating sufficiently attractive careers on this side of the Causeway.

Title: Asteel revamps board after Clifford Hii takes control, ex-IGP named chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asteel Group Bhd has revamped its board following the change in control, appointing former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman.
Asteel's new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong was named executive deputy chairman.
The appointments follow Clifford's acquisition of a 53.08 per cent stake in Asteel at the close of his mandatory general offer on Monday through investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd.
Clifford, 43, emerged as Asteel's controlling shareholder in August after acquiring an initial 52.94 per cent stake for RM20.75 million, or 7.5 sen a share.
The deal triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06 per cent at the same price.
The son of property and education businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, Clifford has more than 20 years' experience spanning education, property and financial technology.
He previously served as a non-independent non-executive director of HCK Capital Group Bhd.
Razarudin, 63, brings more than four decades of experience in law enforcement and national security.
He was Malaysia's 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025 and is also th independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd.
Asteel also appointed Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors.
Former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai was redesignated executive director and chairman emeritus.
Meanwhile, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming and independent directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn resigned, citing personal reasons.
Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd, while Lor, 62, has more than 35 years' experience in financial services.
This includes banking transformation, strategy, governance and risk management.

Title: Neighbour recalls seeing Kuantan student with suspect hours before tragedy [WATCH]
Article:
KUANTAN: A neighbour expressed shock over the death of a 19-year-old student whom she had spotted walking with the male suspect near Jalan Air Putih just hours before the incident.
The woman, in her 40s, who declined to be named, said she saw the pair walking along the main road about 9pm yesterday.
"I saw them last night and was shocked when I was informed about the girl's death about 6am today. I know her as a well-mannered person.
"The victim and three other girls, who study at the polytechnic here, rented two rooms in the three-storey house near my place. I usually see them walking together or taking e-hailing rides to attend classes," she said when met near the victim's rented room today.
The woman said the four girls moved into the house about six months ago and often walked around the neighbourhood in pairs.
"The girls would usually walk to nearby eateries or the supermarket. I am clueless how the murder occurred or why the suspect was present inside the house," she said.
Earlier, it was reported that a female student was found dead, believed to have been strangled following an argument with her boyfriend, at a house in Jalan Air Putih.( https://www.nst.com.my/news/regional/2026/10/1548833/student-found-dead-kuantan-boyfriend-detained)
The suspect has been detained for investigation. Police have yet to disclose the victim's identity.
Checks by the media at the three-storey premises found that it resembled a guesthouse, with several rooms available for long-term rental.
When members of the media went to the premises, they were informed that the parents of the other girls had visited the premises to collect their belongings.

Title: Public trust helped Malaysia navigate subsidy reforms, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's subsidy reforms have proceeded for more than two years, with Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan attributing public acceptance of the changes to fairness and trust in the system.
He said transparency and the government's efforts to balance fiscal needs with support for those requiring assistance had helped secure acceptance of difficult decisions.
"Now the reality is we've now done subsidy rationalisation for more than two years. We still don't have riots in the streets.
"The government seems to have figured out how to do the balancing and actually make it clear that society accepts that it has to make decisions.
"It has to accept that decisions are not always easy, but it accepts them because of the concept of fairness and trust in the system," he said at the Khazanah Megatrends Forum at the Mandarin Oriental Kuala Lumpur here today.
Amir Hamzah said the government had to establish why subsidy reforms were necessary while convincing people that the changes were being implemented fairly.
He said subsidies remained important because society was unequal, with those at the lower end needing support even as better-off groups continued to enjoy a comfortable life.
"The key for the government is to make sure that subsidies don't end up giving things to a person who doesn't deserve to get them, when other people deserve to get them in a better form," he said.
He said the broader challenge was to strengthen Malaysia's finances and fiscal discipline while balancing economic growth with measures to improve people's lives.
Amir Hamzah said the Fiscal Responsibility Act provided safeguards for managing the country's finances, with lower fiscal deficits important to ensuring the government could support future growth.
"We don't want to steal from our children or grandchildren and enjoy the fruits of things today," he added.

Title: Elridge Energy to acquire 6 activated carbon production chains for RM45mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary, Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd is venturing into the manufacture and sale of activated carbon (AC) with the proposed acquisition of six integrated AC production chains for RM45 million.
The biomass fuel manufacturer said it has accepted the quotation issued by United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of the production chains.
"The AC production chains will be installed in Klang, Selangor, and are expected to have an eventual cumulative production capacity up to 21,600 tonnes per annum of AC," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
In a separate statement, Elridge Energy said the investment represents a significant extension of the group's existing palm kernel shell (PKS) business, enabling it to move beyond supplying PKS primarily as biomass fuel and convert the same feedstock into AC.
Executive director and chief executive officer Oliver Yeo said the investment marks an important step in the group's strategy to move further downstream and capture greater value from the PKS supply chain.
"We intend to leverage our existing access to PKS feedstock, logistics capabilities and industry relationships to produce AC, a higher value-added product with applications across water treatment, air purification and a broad range of industrial processes.
"As production ramps up from 2027, we expect the AC business to broaden the group's revenue base and, subject to market conditions and successful execution, contribute positively to the group's future earnings," he added.

Title: KLK: Majority of fires originated from beyond concession area, all have been put out
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) has clarified that cases of fire said to trace back to its Indonesian subsidiary PT Menteng Jaya Sawit Perdana (PT MJSP) actually originated from beyond its oncession area and all have been put out.
The company said as a member of the Roundtable Sustainable Palm Oil, it holds a zero burning policy and does not permit open burning for land preparation or any other purpose across its operations.
"We are aware of current news reports referencing our subsidiary, PT MJSP, in relation to the haze source points detected within its concession area and wish to provide the following clarification.
"The PT MJSP concession is now wholly mature and has no replanting activities.
"Where cases of fire have occurred, the majority of them originated from beyond our concession area and all have been put out," it said in a statement.
Given the exceptionally dry conditions this year, with more than 90 days without rain due to the Super El Niño, KLK said the risk of fire and reignition is significantly higher.
"With the weather forecasted to continue to be dry due to the El Niño, maintaining morale and stamina of our people is our priority."
KLK said its team had enhanced efforts on the ground to put out and contain existing fires, while taking measures to prevent reignition and new fires from occurring.
"This includes large areas beyond our concession. With this exceptionally prolonged dry spell, our team also ran into great risk of fatigue, constantly being alert and battling the hotspots around us.
"Increase of water supply arrangements were made to ensure firefighting operations can continue without interruption.
"This includes purchase of external water source in areas where water supply is limited due to the dry weather, construction of additional water retention ponds, construction of tube walls to strengthen long-term firefighting water availability and permanent deployment of water tankers," said KLK.
The group has also ramped up fire surveillance and hotspot monitoring round the clock with dedicated teams manning satellite hotspot monitoring and drone surveillance, complemented by daily ground patrols across our estates and the surrounding areas.
"All fire incidents are documented and reported to the relevant authorities for further actions, if necessary.
"The situation on the ground remains challenging. Our immediate priority is to suppress fire and reignition in our concession and surrounding areas.
"We remain fully committed to safeguard the community's and our team's safety," it said.

Title: Johor Port eyes Belawan trade link
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Port Bhd is exploring a potential trade corridor linking Johor with Belawan in North Sumatra, as it seeks to strengthen cargo connectivity between Malaysia and Indonesia.
The port operator, a subsidiary of MMC Port Holdings Bhd, said it is working with PT Pelabuhan Indonesia (Persero) Regional 1 Belawan to assess opportunities for more efficient cargo movement, wider market access and stronger trade links between the two markets.
The potential Belawan-Johor connection was discussed during Johor Port's visit to Belawan Port in early September, held in conjunction with the Indonesia-Malaysia-Thailand Growth Triangle (IMT-GT) 2026 programme in Medan.
Johor Port chief executive officer Md Derick Basir said the proposed corridor could bring businesses and markets in Northern Sumatra and Johor closer together.
"This opportunity is more than about connecting the two ports. It is also about bringing businesses and markets closer together, creating more efficient pathways for trade and supporting stronger regional supply chains," he said in a statement today.
He said Johor Port would work with Pelindo and industry stakeholders to identify commercially viable opportunities that could improve connectivity between Northern Sumatra and Johor.
The discussions covered Belawan's port facilities, existing cargo flows, hinterland access, market demand, logistics requirements and potential areas of commercial cooperation.
Belawan is a key gateway to Northern Sumatra, while Johor Port provides access to Johor, the wider Malaysian market and established regional shipping networks.
Johor Port said the proposed connection could handle cargo from sectors including manufacturing, consumer products, industrial goods and other regional trade flows.
However, any new service would depend on sufficient cargo demand, reliable operations and a commercially sustainable structure.
The two sides will continue discussions with shipping lines, logistics providers, cargo owners and the wider business community to identify potential cargo flows and shipping partners.
Johor Port, a multi-purpose port in southern Johor, handles container, dry bulk, break bulk and liquid cargo.
Its container terminal recorded a record annual throughput of 1.08 million TEUs in 2025.
The proposed Belawan-Johor link forms part of Johor Port's broader effort to expand its commercial hinterland and strengthen intra-Asia connectivity.
It also supports the IMT-GT's role in facilitating closer trade and logistics links among Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah student seriously injured after fall from school building
Article:
ALOR STAR: The Kedah Education Department is monitoring the case of a Form One student who was seriously injured after he was believed to have fallen from the third floor of a secondary school in Kulim Bandar Baharu.
The incident occurred on Sunday. The 13-year-old boy is now reportedly conscious and remains under treatment and close observation at a hospital.
In a statement today, the department expressed sympathy to the student and prayed for his recovery.
"Upon receiving information about the incident, the school and the Kulim Bandar Baharu District Education Office took immediate action, including contacting the student's family and lodging a report with the authorities," it said.
Psychosocial support was also provided to the student, his family and schoolmates affected by the incident.
The department said it was also aware of preliminary police findings that the student was believed to have been facing pressure related to his academic performance.
However, investigations into the incident are still ongoing and the department is cooperating fully with the authorities.
"The Education Department takes the emotional and mental wellbeing of students seriously and urges parents and educators to be more alert to changes in their emotions and ensure they receive help promptly," it said.
Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring was earlier reported to have said the student was seriously injured after he was believed to have fallen from the third floor of the school building during recess.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian among 13 held over 521kg meth seizure from private jet in Laos
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police are awaiting more information from Laos police on the seizure of 521kg of methamphetamine from a private jet at Luang Prabang International Airport.
According to Bukit Aman, a Malaysian is believed to be among 13 people detained by Lao authorities following the seizure of the drugs.
The private aircraft arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police have yet to receive detailed information on the case from their Lao counterparts.
"So far, we have not received any information or details from the Lao drug authorities.
"Based on the information we have, one of the 13 people detained is a Malaysian who is believed to have been arrested in Laos," he said when contacted today.
Hussein, however, said the Malaysian was not among those who travelled aboard the private jet from Subang to Laos.
He confirmed that a private jet had flown from Subang to Laos, but said both the pilot and co-pilot were not Malaysians.
Asked whether the case could be linked to the earlier arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia over a drug trafficking case, Hussein said investigations were still ongoing.
"It is under investigation. It is too early for us to say whether there is a connection.
"At this point, the information we have is that a Malaysian has been detained there, but he was not among those who travelled from Malaysia on the flight concerned," he said.
It was reported that Lao police have seized 521 kilogrammes of crystal methamphetamine from a
private jet
reported to have arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 people detained in connection with the case.
The Vientiane Times, citing Lao Security Newspaper , reported on Tuesday that a security operation took place on Oct 1 following a tip-off received by provincial police on Sept 21 that a drug trafficking syndicate was allegedly planning to smuggle narcotics across borders by air using a private aircraft.
According to the report, police later learned that the flight schedule had been changed, with the private aircraft due to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30pm on Oct 1.
Provincial public security authorities then instructed specialised units to monitor the situation.
Officers subsequently found 23 suitcases and seized 500 packs of crystal methamphetamine weighing 521 kilogrammes, along with the Learjet private aircraft and a pickup truck as evidence, according to the report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jaya Grocer warns over Instagram posts offering gold bars, iPhones
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jaya Grocer said its Instagram account had been compromised, warning that posts offering gold bars, iPhones and other prizes were not authorised by the supermarket chain.
The posts, promoting an "Anniversary Promo" and directing users to Telegram, were not part of any promotion run by the company, it said in a social media post.
"Our Instagram account has been compromised. The 'Anniversary Promo' posts offering gold bars, iPhones, and other prizes with a link to Telegram were not posted by us."
"Please do not click any links, message the Telegram account, or make any payments."
Jaya Grocer said it was working to regain control of the account and would provide updates.
It also urged anyone who had responded to the posts to contact their bank immediately and report the incident to police.
Jaya Grocer is a supermarket chain selling fresh produce, groceries and household goods.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Scientex buys 203.6ha in Johor for RM580mil from Lau family
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Scientex Bhd is acquiring 203.6 hectares of land in Pulai, Johor for RM580 million as the affordable housing developer expands its land bank.
The 14 plots, currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd, will be developed into a mixed development, Scientex said in an exchange filing.
The company said it is too early to determine the development value and other details of the proposed project.
The acquisition is expected to create operational efficiencies because the land is close to Scientex's existing projects in the area.
This allows the group to benefit from greater economies of scale, Scientex said in a bourse filing today.
The sale and purchase agreement was signed by Scientex's wholly owned subsidiary Scientex Quatari Sdn Bhd and Pangkal Budiman Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Leong Hup Holdings Sdn Bhd.
Scientex, which also manufactures flexible plastic packaging, has more than 4,451ha across seven states in Peninsular Malaysia.
It aims to build 50,000 affordable homes nationwide by 2028, having delivered about 47,000 homes to date.
The RM580 million acquisition will be financed through a combination of internal funds and bank borrowings and is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027.
As at July 31, 2026, Scientex had RM357.8 million in cash and RM2.05 billion in total borrowings.
Scientex said the land would support a steady and sustainable property development model, with the group continuing to focus on affordably priced landed homes, where demand remains firm and resilient.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah weighs new Mount Kinabalu routes, bans unauthorised trails
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is considering developing new routes on Mount Kinabalu, but climbers will continue to be barred from using trails that have not been authorised by Sabah Parks.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the ministry had been looking into potential routes and areas suitable for exploration even before photographs of less-explored parts of the mountain posted by Croatian climber Mauro Persic went viral.
"We have been looking into the matter for quite some time, including examining routes and places that may be suitable, taking into consideration safety and other factors," he told the media during the 33rd Climbathon press conference at his office here.
Jafry said any decision to develop new routes would also take into account the potential benefits to communities living around Mount Kinabalu.
"Whatever steps we take, what is certain is that the local community and the people of the state must benefit from them," he said.
"We are concerned that using unofficial trails could compromise the safety of climbers," he said.
Last month, Persic, 46, triggered a
five-day search and rescue
operation involving 43 personnel after he climbed through an unauthorised route via Sungai Mesilou without a permit and subsequently fell and sustained injuries.
He was fined the maximum RM25,000 for the offence.
Persic had posted photographs showing parts of Mount Kinabalu away from the authorised routes, prompting curiosity among social media users over whether such areas would be opened to climbers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.
Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).
"From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises," he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank today.
Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule.
He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce the department's workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises.
"In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by the department for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year," he said.
To meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, the department expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide, he said.
He said the fire department currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors.
A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher on positive regional sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended higher today, in line with gains across major Asian markets following Wall Street's overnight technology-led rally, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to temper risk appetite.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.60 points to 1,633.35 from Monday's close of 1,631.75.
The benchmark index, which opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38, moved between 1,632.77 and 1,641.20 throughout the trading session.
On the broader market, gainers surpassed decliners 667 to 456, while 551 counters were unchanged, 1,108 untraded and 13 suspended.
Turnover decreased to 4.18 billion units worth RM2.95 billion, compared with 4.78 billion units worth RM2.89 billion yesterday.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.349 per cent, its highest since 2002, while the 30-year yield briefly reached 5.703 per cent.
At the close on Monday, the S&P 500 gained 0.66 per cent to 7,773.95 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.05 per cent to 27,477.31.
"On a positive note, Brent crude oil eased below US$100 per barrel as resilient West Asia exports and the Group of Seven's (G7) emergency stockpile release helped alleviate supply concerns," he told Bernama.
Domestically, he said buying interest was seen in telecommunications and commodity-related stocks, while trading activity also broadened to selected small-cap technology, energy and plantation counters.
"We believe selected blue chips could continue to attract bargain hunting following last week's sharp correction.
"However, the lack of follow-through buying over the past three sessions suggests investors remain cautious, with persistent foreign selling and elevated bond yields likely to limit the pace of recovery," he said.
Meanwhile, Thong said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 should provide some support to sentiment.
"The 2027 Budget will be tabled on Friday, with strategic sectors including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, energy transition, pharmaceuticals, logistics, and aerospace among the areas highlighted by the government," he said.
For the rest of the week, he expects the benchmark index to remain in consolidation mode, with a mild recovery bias as oversold conditions provide some downside support.
"Nevertheless, a stronger recovery may require fresh catalysts, with Budget 2027, foreign fund flows, bond yields and geopolitical developments remaining key factors to watch.
"We maintain our FBM KLCI trading range of 1,620-1,650 for the week," he added.
Among the heavyweights, IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 15 sen to RM7.91, while Malayan Banking Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhdeased three sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.70, Public Bank Bhd shed four sen to RM4.67, and Tenaga Nasional Bhd slipped 10 sen to RM12.90.

Title: Ringgit ends higher versus greenback ahead of 2027 Budget

Title: Countries weigh banning smart glasses over privacy concerns
Article:
Governments, courts and companies are considering restrictions and examining existing rules on smart glasses amid worries that the technology, brought to mainstream by Meta's Ray-Bans, could be used to photograph, film or audio-record confidential materials or people without their knowledge.
Here is a summary of what countries and regions are doing to protect people's privacy, in alphabetical order.
AUSTRALIA
The federal government said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces due to privacy and security concerns.
Public Service Minister Katy Gallagher asked the country's Public Service Commission for advice on whether their use should be prohibited and what exemptions might be required.
BRITAIN
Courts in England and Wales have prohibited the use of Meta smart glasses because of restrictions on taking images and videos in courts.
British cinema operators are also introducing policies to prohibit ​or restrict camera-enabled smart glasses, the UK Cinema Association said in August.
EUROPEAN UNION
Smart glasses have attracted scrutiny from European privacy regulators and some lawmakers, and the European Data Protection Board has commissioned a report into their "social acceptability."
Member of the European Parliament Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová also urged the European Commission, which has not proposed legislation specifically targeting smart glasses, to consider possible action.
NORWAY
The government said it planned to propose a temporary ban on the use of ​AI glasses in places where the public ​regularly gather, such as parks, beaches, museums, shopping centres and public events.
Norway's capital Oslo banned smart glasses in schools in August.
UNITED STATES
New York's Unified Court System banned smart glasses from all its court facilities from July 20. The rule covers prescription and non-prescription eyewear or headwear containing cameras, microphones, computers or other technology capable of recording video or audio. Visitors carrying them must hand them over to court personnel for safekeeping before entering.
