Title: Nearly 51 years later, daughter of former Perak police chief Khoo Chong Kong remembers the man behind his uniform
Article:
TANJONG MALIM, Oct 6 — Time may have passed, but the image of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Khoo Chong Kong as a loving father and a firm, courageous police officer remains vivid for his daughter, Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim.
Rita, 78, said a pantomime performance held in conjunction with the official opening of the Muallim District Police Headquarters (IPD) today rekindled memories of her father, nearly 51 years after his death, leaving her deeply moved.
“I was 25 at the time and living in Seremban (Negeri Sembilan) after getting married. I received a call from a police officer telling me that something had happened to my father, but I was given no further details.
“When we heard the news, my husband and I rushed back to Ipoh to see my father and find out what had happened to him. He had been attacked with a weapon. I’m really touched that the Royal Malaysia Police, especially the Perak police, still remember him after all these years,” she said when met here today.
Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim (second left), daughter of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Koo Chong Kong, poses with her husband and child beside the original uniform worn by Koo when he was shot dead by communist elements on November 13, 1975, at an exhibition in Ipoh on October 6, 2026. — Bernama pic
Earlier, the Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah officiated the opening of the Muallim IPD.
Rita, Khoo’s eldest daughter, said one of the memories closest to her heart was how devoted her father was to his work, often spending long hours on duty, particularly during his service with the Special Branch and operations to combat communist activities.
She said there were times when her father had to be away from home for one or two months to carry out operations, leaving her mother worried about his safety.
“He was always very busy. There were times when he would leave for an operation and be gone for one or two months. We never knew exactly when he would be coming home,” she said.
Rita said that despite his firm and serious demeanour while on duty, her father was a loving and caring man at home.
Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim, daughter of the late former Perak police chief Tan Sri Koo Chong Kong, speaks during an interview at an exhibition held in conjunction with the opening of the Muallim District Police Headquarters in Ipoh on October 6, 2026. — Bernama pic
She also described him as a man who stood firmly by his principles and would not compromise on what he believed was right, saying his courage in carrying out his duties had always been an inspiration to her.
Meanwhile, Rita said seeing the official car her father once used and the blood-stained uniform he wore during the incident was an emotional experience, bringing back memories of her father and the sacrifice he made in the line of duty.
“It really takes me back to those days. I had seen the car at a museum before, but seeing it again today, together with his uniform and hearing the stories about him, really brought back so many memories,” she said.
Born on November 12, 1925, in Kwangsi, China, the late Khoo was raised in Ipoh and joined the Sarawak Constabulary as an inspector on November 5, 1952, before holding several key positions and eventually becoming Perak police chief on January 7, 1975.
Beside the official car once used by her late father, former Perak police chief Tan Sri Koo Chong Kong, Datin Rita Koo Swee Kim (right) poses with her child at an exhibition in Ipoh on October 6, 2026. Koo was shot dead by communist elements on November 13, 1975. — Bernama pic
He was shot while travelling home from the Perak Police Contingent Headquarters to his residence on Jalan Tawar, Ipoh, at about 1pm on November 13, 1975, in an attack believed to have been carried out by communist insurgents.
His driver, Corporal Yeong Peng Cheong, was also killed in the attack, while Khoo succumbed to his injuries on November 14, 1975, about 28 hours after he was shot. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: IPD is the abbreviation in Malay for Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah (District Police Headquarters).

Title: ‘A happy family?’: Zara Qairina’s stepsister says she never met teen, but regularly viewed photos on social media
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 6 — The stepsister of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir told the Coroner’s Court that she never lived with the teenager and had no first-hand knowledge of how Zara Qairina’s mother cared for and raised her.
Malianah Mahathir, 25, the 81st witness, said she only knew of Zara Qairina’s life and family from social media posts as well as information from her father.
When questioned by lawyer Shahlan Jufri, who represents Zara Qairina’s mother, Malianah said she had seen photographs of the family through the Facebook accounts of Zara Qairina, her mother and her father.
“I only saw them through Facebook posts. I used to stalk their photos all the time. A happy family, right?” she said before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan during today’s inquest proceedings.
She said her father often uploaded family photographs, including ones of Zara Qairina as a baby and pictures of holidays they took together.
When answering questions from Coroner Amir Shah, Malianah confirmed that she had never met or interacted personally with Zara Qairina at any point between the teenager’s birth and her death.
She also acknowledged that all the information she knew about Zara Qairina was obtained from what others had told her, and not from the teenager herself.
Malianah further agreed that her testimony in court concerning unpleasant experiences she had endured was related to Zara Qairina’s mother, and not to experiences with Zara Qairina herself.
The Coroner then asked whether Zara Qairina’s mother had treated her badly every day throughout the period they lived together, to which Malianah replied: “Ah, no.”
When questioned by lawyer Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip, who represents Zara Qairina’s father, Malianah also admitted that when she first moved in with Zara Qairina’s mother, she was initially happy to have a “new mum” and had been treated well.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after the Form One student was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel at 4am.
The inquest proceedings resume tomorrow with new witnesses. — Bernama

Title: Myanmar president to visit Malaysia tomorrow as migrant returns draw rights groups’ warnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Myanmar’s coup leader turned president Min Aung Hlaing will head to Malaysia on Wednesday for a two-day visit, officials said, following Kuala Lumpur’s plan to return thousands of Myanmar immigrants.
The visit comes after a group of nearly 1,500 returnees reached Myanmar on Sunday, with rights groups warning Rohingya refugees could be among those sent back.
Malaysia said about 5,000 Myanmar nationals have agreed to “voluntary” return, but authorities have not commented on the ethnicities of those who have returned.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim “will hold talks with President Min Aung Hlaing on key bilateral issues, including the voluntary, dignified and safe repatriation of Myanmar nationals of all ethnic groups who have been in Malaysia illegally,” Malaysia’s Foreign Affairs Ministry said on Tuesday.
“The Leaders are also expected to review the ongoing efforts undertaken under the Asean mechanisms” for peace in Myanmar, the ministry said in a statement.
Earlier on Tuesday, Anwar told the Malaysian parliament he and other top Malaysian officials “will raise issues towards a solution”.
Growing hostility
Naypyidaw has repatriated nearly 10,000 migrants from Malaysia this year, its state media said on Monday.
Anwar said Myanmar had to “guarantee proper treatment to their own people so that there is no abuse, oppression and violation of human rights”.
“But for me, any country that wants to bring back their people from our country, we welcome that,” Anwar said.
The Malaysian visit will be among Min Aung Hlaing’s most diplomatically significant since Asean leaders froze out Myanmar’s junta following the 2021 coup and ensuing civil war.
But Anwar said last month he would welcome the Myanmar leader to expedite migrant repatriations.
“I want to tell him that we can be friends and trade.
“We can accept Myanmar, but they must accept (their refugees) back,” Anwar said during a podcast interview.
The repatriation plan follows what Malaysia’s human rights commission has called “growing hostility, discriminatory rhetoric and online attacks” against the Rohingya in Muslim-majority Malaysia.
Malaysia hosts more than 215,000 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the United Nations refugee agency, including more than 126,000 Rohingya from Myanmar — its largest refugee community.
The UN and rights groups have raised concerns about the repatriations, with monitors fearing the Rohingya could face a new wave of abuses in Myanmar, where they are denied full citizenship.
Rights advocates view Min Aung Hlaing as the primary architect of a crackdown against the group, starting in 2017, which is being weighed by the International Court of Justice as potential genocide.
‘No time to return’
Myanmar this month pledged “safe and dignified” returns for its citizens displaced abroad.
Myanmar is also riven by violence, with 50 killed last week in a military airstrike on a marketplace in western Rakhine state.
“This is no time to return anyone forcibly to a country plagued by egregious human rights violations and abuses,” UN rights chief Volker Turk said last week.
Min Aung Hlaing ousted the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021, plunging Myanmar into a civil war that has killed more than 100,000 people, according to monitor ACLED.
Since elections that were widely dismissed as a charade, Min Aung Hlaing became civilian leader and launched a drive for regional recognition.
Asean has frozen Myanmar’s top leaders out of its summits since the coup over a lack of engagement with its roadmap to end the civil war.
After 2021, the bloc presented a united front, demanding Myanmar engage with its five-point plan to bring peace through dialogue between all sides.
But analysts have warned the consensus is now fracturing, with some Asean nations now welcoming Min Aung Hlaing.
Malaysia will be the fifth nation of the 11-member Asean bloc – following Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia – to welcome him since taking up the presidency.
He has also visited China – which previously backed him behind the scenes, according to analysts – as well as India and Russia. — AFP

Title: Fishmonger fined RM5,000 for peeping at neighbour in shower
Article:
KUALA KRAI, Oct 6 — The Magistrate’s Court here today fined a fishmonger RM5,000 after he pleaded guilty to peeping at his neighbour’s wife last month.
Magistrate Rais Imran Hamid also ordered Tuan Ahmad Farid Tuan Mat, 36, to serve nine months in prison if he fails to pay the fine.
The man was charged with peeping at the 26-year-old victim while she was taking a bath at a house in Jalan Halimah Guchil here at about 11.30am on September 28, with the intention or knowledge that it would cause fear, anxiety or distress to the victim regarding her safety.
The charge was framed under Section 507A (1) of the Penal Code, punishable under the same section, which carries a maximum prison term of three years or a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Mazlinda Mohd Nor urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence in the public interest and to serve as a lesson to prevent the accused from repeating the offence.
However, counsel Farazalila Fauzi from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), representing Tuan Ahmad Farid, pleaded for a minimum fine on the grounds that her client is single, earns about RM50 daily as a fishmonger, and supports his 66-year-old mother who has cancer.

Title: Ahead of Budget 2027, World Bank tells Putrajaya to raise revenue without raising rates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia needs tax reform to address a structural decline in its tax revenue-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio, which has fallen to 12.7 per cent from 15 per cent 15 years ago, according to the World Bank lead economist Apurva Sanghi.
He said the federal government debt has risen to over 65 per cent of GDP although the fiscal deficit has been contained, however, this would not be enough to bring the debt-to-GDP ratio down to the target of 60 per cent by 2028.
“Federal government debt rose despite the contained deficit and now stands at 65.2 per cent.
“The cost of servicing debt is also increasing, with 17 sen of every ringgit in revenue raised spent on debt servicing,” he told the media during a briefing on October 2026 East Asia and Pacific Economic Update here today.
Yesterday, the Auditor General’s Report 2/2026 reported that federal government debt stood at RM1.32 trillion in 2025 compared with RM1.24 trillion in 2024, while the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills.
Apurva said that while increasing tax rates would be difficult, there were ways to raise tax revenue without doing so.
Responding to a question on taxation and Budget 2027, which will be tabled this Friday, he said simplifying the corporate tax system for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) by consolidating the tax structure would benefit businesses.
“Apart from that, when an SME grows and becomes a non-SME, its favourable tax rate is suddenly taken away. We call this a tax curve, and it reduces the incentive for SMEs to officially grow bigger. As we know, about 98 per cent of Malaysian companies are SMEs. Changing the incentive structure to encourage firms to graduate from SME status can help,” he added.
He also said that it would be good to see the budget make the tax system more supportive of investment.
“To be precise, consider allowing qualifying investments to fully cover 100 per cent of the investment cost,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Socso cuts benefit claim processing time to 2.7 days from 5.3 days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) has reduced the processing time for contributor benefit claims from an average of 5.3 days in 2024 to 2.7 days as of last year.
Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the service delivery improvement was carried out in compliance with the Client Charter to ensure quality standards remain at an optimal level.
He said the initial response time for complaint processing was also shortened from three days in 2024 to just one day in 2025.
“Beginning 2025, the processing time for each benefit application under the Employment Injury Scheme, Self-Employment Social Security Scheme and Housewives’ Social Security Scheme has been reduced from an average of 5.3 days the previous year to 2.7 days in 2025,” he said.
He was responding to a question from V. Ganabatirau (PH-Klang), who asked about reforms to improve Perkeso’s operational efficiency as well as the mismatch between the Invalidity Pension rate and the current cost of living.
He said that from January 1 to December 31, 2025, Perkeso’s Client Charter performance for the overall benefit claim and payment process across the three schemes averaged 96.86 per cent.
Addressing the issue of the Invalidity Pension, Khairul Firdaus said the government does not set pension rates arbitrarily, but rather reviews them periodically every three to five years.
He said these reviews take into account the rising cost of living, inflation rates and the sustainability of the organisation’s funds.
“Indicators and mechanisms for determining increases in the minimum pension rate, implemented by the ministry and Perkeso, are based on actuarial assessment studies by the International Labour Organisation, taking into consideration the current social and economic conditions in our country,” he said.
He added that the findings serve as a key benchmark in ensuring monthly payments are sufficient to help recipients make ends meet. — Bernama
Note: Perkeso is also known as Socso, the English acronym for Social Security Organisation.

Title: Chest a minute! Diner allegedly plucks out body hair and plants it in ‘char kway teow’ to dodge RM30 bill in Penang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — A diner in Penang allegedly plucked hair from his own chest and planted it in a plate of
char kway teow
before claiming the food was contaminated and refusing to pay the RM30 bill.
The alleged ruse was only discovered after the restaurant manager checked CCTV footage, which he said appeared to show the man repeatedly reaching inside his clothes before placing something into the dish.
The incident is believed to have happened at a restaurant along Persiaran Gurney in George Town at about 5pm on Sunday, October 4, according to
Sin Chew Daily
, as reported by
The Star
.
The restaurant manager, identified only as Cheng, said the man, believed to be a foreign national, and his companion had initially wanted to order fried chicken but chose
char kway teow
, an egg and a drink after being told the chicken was sold out.
Cheng said the man later complained that he had found hair in the noodles.
“After examining it, I found that something was amiss,” he was quoted as saying.
“If the hair had really been in the
char kway teow
, it should have been oily, but the hair we found was dry.
“There were six to seven strands of hair in the dish. They were also very short and did not look like eyelashes.”
Cheng said the couple then got up to leave while restaurant staff were still examining the food.
When reminded that they had not paid, the man allegedly refused, saying he would not pay for food that had been contaminated.
Suspicious, Cheng later reviewed the restaurant’s CCTV footage.
He claimed the recording appeared to show the man repeatedly putting his hand inside his clothes, pulling out what looked like chest hair and placing it into the
char kway teow
.
The meal cost about RM30.
Cheng said the CCTV footage had since been shared with other restaurant operators to warn them about the couple.

Title: KLIA incident involving border agency chief: AGC to examine witness statements, evidence before deciding on further action
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will examine witness statements, closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and various other evidence before deciding on further action in connection with an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said this after the AGC confirmed receiving the investigation papers on the case, which occurred at Terminal 1 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28.
He said all evidence gathered during the investigation would be thoroughly examined to enable the AGC to determine the next course of action.
“The AGC will examine every aspect of the investigation before any further action can be taken in connection with this case,” he said when contacted today.
Yesterday, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the investigation papers had been submitted to the AGC for review, advice and further directions in accordance with Article 145(3) of the Federal Constitution.
So far, 25 witnesses have had their statements recorded to assist in the investigation.
The investigation is being conducted by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which covers the offence of voluntarily causing hurt, illness or bodily weakness to another person.
Mohd Shuhaily had previously said that he left it to the government to decide on any action that might be taken against him following a viral video showing him reprimanding two individuals at KLIA Terminal 1. — Bernama

Title: Johor Regent receives MACC chief, new state director at Istana Pasir Pelangi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail granted an audience to Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman at Istana Pasir Pelangi yesterday.
According to a statement posted on His Royal Highness’ official Facebook page, the new Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid, whose appointment took effect on October 1, was also present during the audience.
“During the meeting, the MACC leadership conveyed the agency’s continued commitment to strengthening anti-corruption enforcement and prevention, as well as integrity and governance in the state.
“The meeting reflects the continuing working relationship between the MACC and the Johor Royal Institution in supporting the agenda of integrity and good governance,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: E-hailing driver tests positive for meth after crash kills 22-year-old Maldivian student near PJS toll
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Oct 6 — An e-hailing driver tested positive for methamphetamine in a urine screening test after a crash on the New Pantai Expressway (NPE) that killed a 22-year-old female student from the Maldives,
Harian Metro
reported.
The 37-year-old driver was carrying two Maldivian women when his Perodua Ativa collided with a Proton S70 near the PJS Toll Plaza at about 8.48pm on Sunday, according to Subang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat.
Police said the Ativa spun and overturned in the middle of the road following the impact.
“One of the passengers was trapped in the vehicle and pronounced dead at the scene, while the other was injured,” Wan Azlan was quoted as saying.
Both women, aged 22, were students at a private higher education institution in the Klang Valley.
According to police investigations, the Proton S70, driven by a 34-year-old local man, was heading towards the RFID lane when the rear right side of the car was struck by the Ativa from the right.
Wan Azlan said urine screening tests were carried out on both drivers following the crash.
The e-hailing driver tested positive for methamphetamine, also known locally as syabu, he said.
A Shah Alam Magistrates’ Court subsequently granted police a four-day remand order against the driver to assist investigations.
“The case is being investigated under Section 44(1)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, and the investigation papers are expected to be submitted to the Deputy Public Prosecutor tomorrow for further instructions,” Wan Azlan said.
The body of the victim was taken to the Serdang Hospital Forensic Department for a post-mortem examination.
Police have urged witnesses or motorists with dashcam footage of the crash to contact investigating officer Inspector Azizul Hakim Roslan at 011-2891 4495 or the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Subang Jaya district police headquarters.

Title: Three crocodiles, including 4.75m giant, captured in Sarawak’s Batang Igan
Article:
SIBU, Oct 6 — Three large-sized crocodiles measuring between 2.44 metres and 4.75 metres were captured within the last three days in Sungai Batang Igan near Ulu Kampung Kebuaw, Igan, near here.
Licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong said the largest of the three, measuring 4.75 metres and estimated to weigh 500 kilogrammes, was captured at about 2.30am today by his four-member team with the assistance of villagers.
“The residents sought our help following frequent sightings of crocodiles in the area, including an incident in which one attacked a pet dog, causing concern among the villagers.
“After the crocodile was captured, the residents also helped us lift it onto the boat,” he told Bernama today.
Jeferry said the operation in the area began on October 3, with three crocodiles captured so far.
Two crocodiles measuring about 2.44 metres and 2.74 metres respectively were captured on October 4 and 5, before the largest, measuring 4.75 metres, was captured.
He said his team also found a nest containing about 40 crocodile eggs while conducting the operation.
Jeferry expressed his appreciation to the residents of Kampung Kebuaw for their cooperation and teamwork throughout the operation, as well as to Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) for its cooperation.
He said since obtaining a licence to hunt the reptile two years ago, he had captured over 100 crocodiles. — Bernama

Title: ‘She should not wait any longer’: High Court rejects bid to delay RM1.48m condo prize for Miss Asia Malaysia 2023 winner
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Miss Asia Malaysia 2023 winner Luwe Xin Hui can proceed with enforcing a court order for a RM1.48 million condominium, or its cash equivalent, after the High Court rejected an attempt by the pageant organiser to put the ruling on hold pending an appeal.
High Court judge Datuk Arik Sanusi Yeop Johari said Luwe should not be made to wait any longer for the grand prize she was promised after winning the pageant three years ago, the
New Straits Times
reported.
The judge dismissed an application by Asia Television Digital Media (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to stay the execution of an earlier ruling in Luwe’s favour.
On January 29, the High Court granted Luwe summary judgment and ordered the company to transfer and register in her name a unit at Picasso Residence in Jalan Ampang worth RM1.48 million, together with vacant possession and the keys.
The company was also ordered to bear the relevant costs, stamp duty and legal expenses.
If the transfer could not be completed, the court ordered the company to pay Luwe RM1.48 million in cash instead.
In his grounds of judgment, Arik said Luwe was entitled to the grand prize represented and promised by the company as the pageant’s main organiser.
He noted that although Luwe was crowned in 2023, she had still not received the property by the time she filed her lawsuit in 2025.
“However, since the plaintiff was announced as the champion of the pageant in 2023 until this action was filed in 2025, the defendant had failed, refused and neglected to deliver the grand prize to the plaintiff.
“Since the defendant had failed, refused, and neglected to deliver the grand prize worth RM1.48 million to the plaintiff, it is appropriate, as an alternative, for the defendant to remedy the situation and pay damages of RM1.48 million, equivalent to the value of the condominium, to the plaintiff,” he said.
The court also ordered the company to pay RM5,000 in costs.
In seeking a stay, Asia Television Digital Media argued that the condominium remained registered in the name of developer Premier De Muara Sdn Bhd and that transferring the unit would involve several procedural steps as well as additional costs and expenses.
It also argued that being required to pay Luwe RM1.48 million in cash could leave it facing substantial difficulty in recovering the money if its appeal ultimately succeeded.
Arik rejected those arguments, ruling that they did not amount to the “special circumstances” required to justify a stay of execution.
He said the company’s concern that it might not be able to recover the RM1.48 million was speculative.
“The court is of the view that this reason does not constitute a special circumstance which justifies a stay of execution of the judgment,” he said.
The judge also rejected the company’s argument that allowing Luwe to enforce the judgment would render its appeal nugatory or academic.
“If the defendant succeeds in its appeal later, the defendant may recover the RM1.48 million from the plaintiff and this would not prejudice or deny the defendant’s rights to the money,” he said.
The company filed its notice of appeal on February 26.
Luwe was represented by Chew Wee Kian and Ee Pei Ying, while Marcus Teoh and Doris Na acted for the company.

Title: Monsoon transition begins Oct 9, bringing thunderstorms, flash flood and fallen tree risks, MetMalaysia warns
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The monsoon transition phase is expected to begin on October 9 and continue until late October, marking the end of the South-west Monsoon, which began on May 14.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said in a statement today that during this phase, the country will experience weak winds blowing from various directions, which are conducive to the formation of thunderstorm clouds.
“This situation typically brings heavy rain and lightning accompanied by strong winds over a short period, particularly during the afternoon and early evening in most areas in the west and interior of the Peninsula, as well as western Sabah and Sarawak.
“These weather phenomena have the potential to cause flash floods, water surges, fallen trees, and damage to unstable structures,” he said.
He added that with the end of the South-west Monsoon, transboundary haze from neighbouring countries is expected to gradually diminish following changes in wind patterns.
As such, the public is advised to exercise greater caution during this period and stay informed about weather forecasts and warnings issued by METMalaysia through its official website, myCuaca mobile application, and official social media platforms.
The public can also contact the department’s hotline at 1-300-22-1638 for further enquiries, he said. — Bernama

Title: Nineteen-year-old motorcyclist killed in three-vehicle crash in Sepang
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 6 — A 19-year-old girl was killed after the motorcycle she was riding was involved in a collision with another motorcycle and a car on Jalan Sepang/Salak at about 8.20pm yesterday.
Sepang police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said the victim, who was riding a blue Honda C100, was believed to have collided with a black Honda C100 motorcycle travelling from Sungai Pelek towards Nilai.
“The black motorcycle is believed to have collided with the blue motorcycle, which at that time was travelling against the flow of traffic in the left lane of the same road. Following the collision, the woman was thrown off her motorcycle and landed in the right lane before she was believed to have been run over by a grey Proton Saga Iswara travelling straight in the right lane.
“The victim was pronounced dead at the scene by an assistant medical officer. The victim worked at a cattle farm in the Sepang area and did not possess a valid driving licence,” he said in a statement today.
Norhizam said the rider of the black motorcycle was an Indian national who worked as a cook at an eatery and was also found not to have a valid driving licence.
Meanwhile, the car driver, a man in his 20s, works as a food and beverage sector supervisor and holds a valid driving licence.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless or dangerous driving resulting in death.
Norhizam urged those who witnessed the incident or have any information related to the case to visit any nearby police station or to contact investigating officer Insp Mohamad Fadzil Zainol Abidin at 019-5588221 or 03-87774264.
He also advised the public against making any speculation regarding the incident to avoid interfering with police investigation. — Bernama

Title: Labuan water disruption enters third day, forcing eateries to halt operations
Article:
LABUAN, Oct 6 — Thousands of consumers in more than 20 villages and residential areas across Labuan are grappling with a water supply disruption for the third consecutive day today, forcing several food and beverage operators to suspend business activities.
The disruption, which began on Sunday (October 4), has affected households, restaurants, eateries and other commercial establishments, leaving business operators struggling to maintain daily operations amid uncertainty over when the supply will be fully restored.
Food and beverage operators have been particularly affected, with the prolonged interruption hampering essential activities such as food preparation, dishwashing and kitchen sanitation, all of which require a continuous supply of clean water.
Saadiah Said, 49, said the disruption had severely affected her business, leaving her with no choice but to temporarily close her eatery until the water supply was restored.
“We depend heavily on water for almost everything, from preparing food and washing dishes to maintaining cleanliness in the kitchen. Without water, it is simply impossible for us to operate as usual.
“This is already the third day, and we are losing our daily income while still having to bear operating expenses. We hope the authorities can resolve the problem as soon as possible,” she said.
Another food and beverage operator, Nordi Amirul, 35, said the prolonged disruption was placing a financial strain on small businesses that depend heavily on daily sales to sustain their operations.
“We understand that technical problems can happen, but going three days without a proper water supply is very difficult for small businesses like ours.
“We have customers coming in, but we cannot serve them because there is no water for cooking and cleaning.
“Each day of closure adds to our losses, and we hope measures can be taken to ensure such disruptions do not happen again,” he said.
Meanwhile, the Labuan Water Supply Department (JBAL), in its latest notice issued today, said repair works on the Phase Two Raw Water Pump (RWP) at the Lawa Gadong Water Treatment Plant in Beaufort, Sabah, were still ongoing.
The department said further inspections carried out by the plant operator as of 5am today detected cracks in the pump's bearing casing, requiring repair or replacement to ensure the pump could operate safely and reliably.
“The operator is currently making efforts to obtain a suitable replacement bearing casing to enable repair works to continue as soon as possible,” it said in the notice.
According to JBAL, the disruption has affected almost the entire Federal Territory of Labuan, except for the Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) District Metered Area (DMA).
The disruption stemmed from a malfunction at the Lawa Gadong facility, which forms part of Labuan’s main water supply system and supplies treated water to the island.
Apart from disrupting business activities, the water shortage has also caused considerable inconvenience to households, particularly families that rely on a consistent water supply for cooking, washing, cleaning and other essential daily needs.
JBAL said it would continue monitoring the progress of repair works and provide regular updates to consumers, including an estimated restoration timeline once further information becomes available.
However, no specific timeframe for the full restoration of supply has been announced.
The department expressed regret over the inconvenience caused and appealed for consumers’ patience and understanding while restoration efforts continue.
The prolonged disruption has also highlighted Labuan’s dependence on water supply infrastructure located in mainland Sabah, particularly the Lawa Gadong facility, where operational problems can have widespread implications for consumers and businesses across the island.
Meanwhile, the Public Works Department, Labuan Corporation and JBAL have mobilised water tankers to deliver water to affected villages and residential areas across the island, helping to meet residents’ essential daily needs during the prolonged disruption.
The agencies are coordinating the distribution of water to affected communities while repair works at the Lawa Gadong Water Treatment Plant are ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Kedah MACC detains senior govt officer, two others over suspected RM155,000 graft in sports attire supply
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 6 — The Kedah Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained three individuals, including a senior officer from a government agency, on suspicion of giving and receiving bribes amounting to approximately RM155,000.
According to an MACC source, the other two individuals, a civil servant and a company owner are suspected of accepting the bribes in exchange for approving a quotation for the supply of sports attire.
“The suspects, comprising two men and a woman aged in their 40s and 50s, were detained between 5pm and 9pm yesterday while present to give statements at the Kedah MACC office.
“Preliminary investigations revealed that all the suspects allegedly conspired to commit the act between 2024 and 2025,” the statement read.
It added that initial investigations indicated the two civil servant suspects had received the bribes both in cash and via money transfers to their respective personal bank accounts.
Meanwhile, Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong confirmed the arrests when contacted and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009.
A five-day remand order against all the suspects, valid until October 10, was issued following an application by the MACC at the Magistrate's Court here this morning. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya autonomous EV bus service starts this week: Six stops, RM1 per ride
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Putrajaya’s Nadiputra public bus service will be joined by an autonomous electric bus starting tomorrow, October 7, 2026. Operated in collaboration with Handal Indah and eMooVit (remember this 5G-connected autonomous Proton Exora?), the new self-driving EV bus service will serve Route P113, connecting MRT Putrajaya Sentral to Dataran Gemilang.
From what we can gather, the service will likely use eMooVit’s Kinglong EV bus, which the company has been operating since 2022. The autonomous EV bus has performed numerous demo and test runs over the years, including on the Sunway BRT Line with Rapid KL, as well as in Cyberjaya and Putrajaya itself.
At the moment, it is unclear whether this will be a permanent service. However, official records show that Perbadanan Putrajaya issued a tender last December for an autonomous EV bus service with an 18-month duration, which was eventually awarded to Handal Indah with a final value of RM779,770.
Route stops and operating hours
Our close encounter with the eMooVit autonomous EV bus, in front of Yinson GreenTech (YGT) Cyberjaya’s office in 2024. YGT is a major shareholder of eMooVit. — SoyaCincau pic
The new Route P113 service runs a loop starting and ending at MRT Putrajaya Sentral, covering key administrative hubs along the way:
MRT Putrajaya Sentral (Start)
Kementerian Kewangan
Istana Kehakiman
Kementerian Belia & Sukan
Dataran Gemilang
Kompleks Perbadanan Putrajaya (PPJ)
MRT Putrajaya Sentral (End)
Currently, the operational hours of the autonomous EV bus appear to be rather limited. The service will operate strictly from Monday to Friday and will not run on Saturdays, Sundays, or Public Holidays.
Departure times from MRT Putrajaya Sentral are listed below, subject to traffic conditions:
Morning:
7.15am | 8.15am | 9.15am | 10.15am
Afternoon:
2.45pm | 3.45pm | 4.45pm | 5.45pm
No Touch ‘n Go or My50 support?
The announcement on Perbadanan Putrajaya’s Facebook page, as captured at 3.15pm. — SoyaCincau pic
Aside from its limited operating hours, another detail that caught our attention in the Facebook announcement is the payment method. While the P113 autonomous EV bus service accepts cashless payments, passengers must use a Visa or Mastercard credit or debit card to pay for the ride.
This differs from standard Rapid KL and Nadiputra bus rides, which accept Touch ‘n Go cards and Rapid Passes/MY50. As for the fare, it costs RM1 per ride to travel on the new autonomous EV bus service. —
SoyaCincau

Title: Melaka International Cruise Terminal piling works reach 56pc, says CM
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 6 — Piling works for the Melaka International Cruise Terminal (MICT) project on Pulau Melaka here have reached 56 per cent completion, with 170 piles installed as of October 3.
Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the remaining 134 piles are expected to be installed by mid-November, and the MICT project development comprises several key components, including an L-shaped jetty, a T-shaped jetty, and a Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) complex.
“For the ‘L’-shaped jetty component, the developer aims to complete construction by the end of next year before operations commence in early 2028, while the ‘T’-shaped jetty and the CIQ Complex are expected to be completed in 2029.
“The development of the MICT jetty holds immense potential for Melaka as it directly aligns with the state’s strengths as a tourism destination, particularly in expanding the international cruise tourism market,” he told reporters at Pulau Melaka here today.
The visit was also attended by KAJ Development Sdn Bhd (KAJD) executive chairman Datuk Daing A Malek Daing A Rahaman.
Ab Rauf said the MICT development would open another international maritime gateway to Melaka, thereby paving the way for a greater number of international cruise ship arrivals and tourists to the state in the future.
He noted that, based on the presented plans, MICT is expected to accommodate approximately 800 cruise ship arrivals with a capacity of up to 1.6 million passengers annually, involving a total investment value of RM2 billion and the potential to create over 10,000 job opportunities.
“Currently, we receive 4,800 tourists every Monday and 3,000 tourists every Thursday arriving via the Genting Dream Cruise.
“We see the potential of the Blue Economy in this area; the Private Finance Initiative (PFI) collaboration with KAJD is expected to yield significant economic returns for Melaka,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said the state government would continue to ensure that all matters requiring action from departments and agencies are well-coordinated to facilitate the project’s development.
He added that the developer is also expected to ensure that every component of the project is developed in accordance with the agreed technical specifications, safety standards, and timelines.
MICT is a key component of the Melaka Gateway development and it is set to become the largest cruise ship terminal in South-east Asia, thereby playing a pivotal role in the state’s maritime transport industry. — Bernama

Title: Company director in Johor lorry chase case claims trial on attempted murder charge
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 6 — A 39-year-old company director linked to a 100km police chase involving a stolen lorry claimed trial in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of attempted murder.
The accused, Chai Min Quan, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out to him in Malay before Judge N. Kanageswari.
According to the charge, Chai allegedly attempted to murder Noorulamin Soriani, 44, by ramming into him with a black Mitsubishi Triton at 8am on September 30.
The charge was framed under Section 307 of the Penal Code.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Fatihah Mohd Nizam prosecuted, while Chai was represented by lawyer Yap Che Kai.
The court granted Chai bail of RM10,000, subject to three additional conditions: that he report to a police station near his residence, surrender his passport and refrain from harassing the alleged victim or witnesses.
The court fixed November 18 for the submission of documents and case mention.
Earlier, in the Magistrate’s Court, Chai and factory worker Low Boon Lai, 37, pleaded not guilty to a charge of stealing a lorry after the charge was read out to them in Malay before Magistrate A. Shaarmini.
Low also faced separate charges in the same court of obstructing a police officer in the discharge of his duties, dangerous driving and drug possession.
Last Wednesday, footage circulated on social media showing a man driving a lorry dangerously while fleeing several police patrol cars.
Police were subsequently reported to have pursued the lorry for two hours over a distance of about 100km after two suspects allegedly stole the heavy vehicle in Plentong.

Title: PAS president Hadi Awang visits Dr Hasmah’s grave in Putrajaya, received by Mukhriz
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang visited the grave of Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali in Putrajaya today, just over a week after the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad died at the age of 100.
Abdul Hadi shared photographs of the visit to the Pusara Negara in Precinct 20 in a Facebook post, where he also offered prayers for the late physician and public figure.
“May Allah SWT bestow His mercy upon her soul, forgive all her sins, accept all her good deeds, and place her among His faithful and righteous servants, granting her an honoured place by His side.
“Al-Fatihah,” he wrote.
Dr Hasmah’s son, Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, was also at the cemetery and received Abdul Hadi during the visit.
Abdul Hadi was accompanied by his political secretary, Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman.
Dr Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute in Kuala Lumpur on September 28 at the age of 100. She was laid to rest later that day at Pusara Negara following a state funeral attended by Dr Mahathir, their children and other family members.
Born in Klang in 1926, Dr Hasmah was among Malaysia’s pioneering women doctors and built a career in maternal and child healthcare before becoming widely known for her public health and welfare work.
She became the first woman appointed as a medical officer in the Maternal and Child Health Department in 1965 and later the first woman to serve as a state maternal and child health officer.
She was also active in campaigns against drug abuse and held roles in welfare and sporting organisations, while remaining a prominent public figure during Dr Mahathir’s decades in Malaysian politics.

Title: Two men claim trial to Johor lorry theft after 100km police chase; one faces three more charges
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 6 — A company director and a factory worker claimed trial in the Magistrate’s and Sessions Courts here today to charges including the theft of a lorry, dangerous driving, obstructing a police officer and drug possession.
Chai Min Quan, 39, and Low Boon Lai, 37, pleaded not guilty after the lorry theft charge was read to them in Malay by a court interpreter before Magistrate A. Shaarmini.
According to the charge, the two men allegedly stole a CD45-model lorry belonging to Max Theu Zhi Wei from a parking area in front of the BHP Plentong petrol station along Jalan Mutiara 4, Taman Plentong, Masai, near here, at 7.40am on September 30.
They were charged under Section 379A of the Penal Code for motor vehicle theft, which carries a prison term of between one and seven years and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Eizlan Azhar prosecuted, while Chai was represented by lawyer Yap Che Kai. Low was unrepresented.
The court set October 23 for the submission of documents and for Low to appoint a lawyer.
Both men were granted bail of RM7,000 each, with additional conditions requiring them to report to a nearby police station, surrender their international passports and refrain from interfering with the victim or witnesses.
Separately, Low pleaded not guilty before Magistrate Atifah Hazimah Wahab to two further charges, which were read to him in Mandarin.
On the first charge, he is accused of intentionally obstructing Corporal Muhammad Nazmi Ihsan Abdullah from carrying out his duties within the jurisdiction of the Pasir Putih police station at 8.25am on September 30.
He was charged under Section 186 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison term of two years, a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
On the second charge, Low is accused of possessing 0.7g of methamphetamine by the roadside along Jalan Mawar Biru in the Pasir Gudang Industrial Area at 10.20am on the same day.
The charge was framed under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries a maximum prison term of five years, a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Siti Aisyah Mustapha Kamal prosecuted, while Low was unrepresented.
The court set October 23 for the submission of documents in the obstruction case and granted Low bail of RM3,500.
Magistrate Atifah set December 7 for the submission of the chemistry report in the drug possession case and granted him bail of RM3,000.
In a related case, Low pleaded not guilty before Magistrate Nur Fatin Mohamad Farid to a charge of dangerous driving, which was also read to him in Mandarin.
He is accused of driving against the flow of traffic and making an illegal U-turn in a manner that endangered the public along Jalan Mawar Biru at 10.20am on September 30.
He was charged under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum five-year prison term and a fine of RM5,000, as well as the revocation of his driving licence upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by Johor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department prosecuting officer Inspector S. Vikineswary. Low was unrepresented.
The court set November 5 for the submission of documents and granted him bail of RM5,000.
Last Wednesday, footage circulated on social media showing a man driving a lorry dangerously while fleeing several police patrol cars.
Police later said they had pursued the lorry for about two hours over a distance of 100 kilometres after two suspects allegedly stole the heavy vehicle in Plentong.

Title: Laos seizes 521kg of crystal meth from private jet arriving from Malaysia
Article:
PHNOM PENH, Oct 6 — Lao police have seized 521 kilogrammes of crystal methamphetamine from a private jet reported to have arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 people detained in connection with the case.
The Vientiane Times, citing Lao Security Newspaper, reported on Tuesday that a security operation took place on October 1 following a tip-off received by provincial police on September 21 that a drug trafficking syndicate was allegedly planning to smuggle narcotics across borders by air using a private aircraft.
According to the report, police later learned that the flight schedule had been changed, with the private aircraft due to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30pm on October 1.
Provincial public security authorities then instructed specialised units to monitor the situation.
Officers subsequently found 23 suitcases and seized 500 packs of crystal methamphetamine weighing 521 kilogrammes, along with the Learjet private aircraft and a pickup truck as evidence, according to the report.
“Twenty-one of the 23 suitcases contained white crystalline substances that were identified as crystal methamphetamine,” the report said.
Police detained 13 people during the operation, including the pilot, co-pilot, a foreign tourist, three employees of a company and seven employees of Luang Prabang International Airport. Three of those detained were women.
The seized aircraft was identified as a Learjet with flight registration N73GP. — Bernama

Title: Exams board director: MPT4 aims to identify learning weaknesses before pupils reach secondary school
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The Year Four Learning Matrix (MPT4) gives schools a crucial two-year window to address learning gaps through targeted interventions before students enter secondary school.
Examination Board (LP) director Abdul Aziz Mamat said the assessment was designed to help teachers identify and address students’ weaknesses as early as Year Five.
He said the assessment data would enable schools to implement targeted interventions, such as strengthening teaching and learning (PdP) processes, providing remedial support to students who have yet to master basic skills, and offering enrichment activities for those who have already mastered them.
“This gives us at least two years at the primary school level to implement intervention programmes to improve students’ performance and abilities, while also nurturing the potential of those who have already met the established standards.
“This approach allows interventions to be implemented based on students’ needs, rather than comparisons between students or schools,” he said in a video recording shared by the Ministry of Education (MOE) on X today.
MPT4, which is being implemented for the first time this year, involves more than 400,000 Year Four pupils nationwide and will run for three days until Thursday.
The assessment covers four core subjects, namely Bahasa Melayu, English, Mathematics and Science, as well as Chinese and Tamil for pupils at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan.
It is designed to assess pupils’ mastery of basic literacy, numeracy and scientific skills acquired from Year One to Year Four.
To ensure that the interventions do not remain merely “on paper”, Abdul Aziz said responsibility for monitoring and quality assurance was not borne solely by teachers, but was shared across all levels of the education system.
He said teachers were responsible for identifying learning needs and planning interventions, while school administrators were responsible for ensuring that follow-up measures were properly planned and implemented.
Abdul Aziz added that at the district and state levels, LP, together with the relevant MOE divisions, would conduct quality assurance to ensure support and interventions were implemented fairly and effectively. — Bernama

Title: Nearly 9,500 buildings across Malaysia must appoint fire safety managers from April 2027, Bomba D-G says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.
Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).
“From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today.
Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule.
He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises.
“In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said.
Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide.
He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors.
A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony. — Bernama

Title: Immigration D-G says Myanmar repatriations will continue beyond initial 5,000
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The repatriation of Myanmar refugees will continue once the 5,000 individuals agreed upon by the Myanmar government have been sent home, said Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban.
Speaking at a press conference on a special operation here today, Zakaria said 1,476 individuals were repatriated in the first phase last month, while more than 3,000 remain in the country.
“This is an ongoing process. It does not stop at just these 5,000. We have not set a quota. If possible, we want them all to return,” he said.
Based on UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) records of issued cards, the number of registered refugees in the country now exceeds 200,000, with nearly half estimated to be Myanmar nationals, he said.
On September 29, Malaysia carried out the first phase of the repatriation programme involving 1,476 Myanmar detainees aboard three vessels, including a Myanmar Navy hospital ship.
The repatriated group comprised 1,370 men, 79 women, 20 boys and seven girls, aged between eight and 60.
Zakaria said the Immigration Department is still awaiting feedback from Wisma Putra regarding further negotiations with the Myanmar authorities for the second phase.
Meanwhile, Zakaria said the exact number of refugees in Malaysia has yet to be determined, and the department is relying on data from UNHCR-issued cardholders.
“I cannot give an estimate, which is why we are implementing the DPP (Refugee Registration Document). The main purpose of the DPP is to determine the actual number of refugees in our country,” he said.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah was previously reported as saying that the DPP, the official registration system for refugees, was implemented early this year.
The initiative was carried out to address security risks and irregular data issues, in line with National Security Council Directive No. 23. — Bernama

Title: ECRL to deploy 200 auxiliary police after RM4m in cable theft losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Some 200 auxiliary police personnel will be deployed at East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) hotspots from November as part of tighter security measures against cable theft and to ensure smooth rail operations.
Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said detection devices, alarm systems and closed-circuit television cameras had also been installed, while security guards and enforcement agencies were being engaged.
“Throughout the construction of the ECRL, we suffered losses of about RM4 million due to cable theft, including three cases last month,” he said at an ECRL operational readiness briefing for media editors today.
Darwis said MRL, as the project and asset owner, remained confident that the ECRL could begin operations by mid-December 2026, based on positive results from System Integration Testing (SIT).
He said progress in the testing and commissioning phase had allowed Fault-Free Runs (FFR) involving Electric Multiple Units (EMUs) for passenger services and electric locomotives (E-Locos) for freight services to begin this month, a month ahead of schedule, without compromising safety or quality.
Meanwhile, Darwis welcomed the agreement between the governments of Malaysia and China on the proposed 30km extension of the ECRL from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang.
He said the extension was expected to reuse about 18km of Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) tracks between Pasir Mas and Rantau Panjang, which have been out of service since 2005.
“The project will facilitate the movement of cargo from southern Thailand to Malaysia, while allowing us to explore the potential of extending the line,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the proposed extension following his recent working visit to China, saying it could connect Malaysia’s rail network with Thailand’s east coast rail system and strengthen links within the wider Pan-Asian rail network.
ECRL Operation Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Zaidi Sharif, meanwhile, said its E-Loco freight service had attracted strong interest from major companies seeking to reduce transport costs and their carbon footprint.
“The E-Loco service will not operate on a fixed timetable but according to demand from companies requiring freight services, which will operate at night,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Jaya Grocer warns customers after Instagram account hacked, fake ‘Anniversary Promo’ posts push Telegram links
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Jaya Grocer has warned customers not to respond to fake promotional posts offering gold bars, iPhones and other prizes after its Instagram account was compromised.
The supermarket chain said the posts, which purported to advertise an “Anniversary Promo” and directed users to a Telegram account, were not published by the company.
“Jaya Grocer is not running these promotions,” it said in a notice on its official Facebook page.
The company urged members of the public not to click on any links contained in the posts, contact the Telegram account or make any payments.
Those who have already responded to the posts were advised to contact their banks immediately and lodge a police report.
Jaya Grocer said it was working to regain control of its Instagram account and would issue further updates once available.
“We are working to regain control of the account and will provide updates as soon as possible,” it said.

Title: Government to define Orang Asli advisory council powers in Act 134 amendments, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The role and responsibilities of the Peninsular Malaysia Orang Asli Advisory Council will be finalised through amendments to the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 (Act 134), which will be tabled in Parliament soon.
Deputy Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang said the council currently operates as a committee that serves as an engagement platform between the government, the Orang Asli community, and relevant non-governmental organisations.
“The establishment (of the council) will be finalised in the amendments to the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 (Act 134), which we will table in Parliament in the near future.
“There, we will detail the role and responsibilities of the council in full,” she said during the Question-and-Answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
She was replying to a supplementary question from Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) regarding the functions and jurisdiction of the council, as well as the steps taken by the government to ensure its views are translated into the formulation and enhancement of policies related to Orang Asli interests.
On the socio-economic development of the Orang Asli community, Rubiah said the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) provides entrepreneur grants ranging from RM9,000 to RM35,000. It also offers cooperative grants of up to RM200,000 to support business equipment and premises.
She added that the government also offers agricultural modernisation programmes with financing from RM5,000 to RM300,000. These programmes cover a broad range of assistance.
“In this regard, we hope the Orang Asli will continue submitting applications to ensure sustainable income generation and expand the local economy holistically,” she said. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in six states until 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Perak, Sarawak and Sabah until 4pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covered Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Yan, Kota Setar and Kuala Muda in Kedah, as well as Kerian in Perak, while the whole of Penang and Perlis were affected.
In Sarawak, the areas involved are Matu, Dalat and Mukah in Mukah; Tatau and Bintulu in Bintulu; Subis, Miri and Marudi in Miri; Lundu in Kuching; and Limbang.
In Sabah, the affected areas are Tambunan, Membakut, Keningau and Beaufort in the Interior; Ranau, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Papar and Kota Belud on the West Coast; Kalabakan, Tawau and Lahad Datu in Tawau; and Kota Marudu in Kudat. — Bernama

Title: Schoolgirl ‘taken away by man on motorcycle’ was hiding in toilet after row, Kulim police say
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — An alarming claim that an 11-year-old girl had left her school with a man on a motorcycle was fabricated by a fellow pupil after a dispute between the pair, police have said.
Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said investigations found the girl had never left the school grounds and had instead hidden inside a toilet after an argument with a friend,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
Police were alerted after the school’s Senior Assistant for Student Affairs received information from two female pupils claiming the girl had left the premises with a man on a motorcycle.
But investigators later established that the account was false.
“Investigations found that the pupil arrived at school as usual at 7.20am after being dropped off by her older sister and attended the school assembly at about 8am,” Syamsul said.
“During the assembly, the pupil was believed to have played with her friend’s hair bun before the friend pulled her headscarf, causing her inner scarf to come off.”
Syamsul said the 11-year-old then went to the toilet to fix her headscarf, but remained there instead of returning to class.
While she was missing from the classroom, one of her friends told the school’s Senior Assistant for Student Affairs that the girl had left the school grounds with a man on a motorcycle.
“However, during questioning, her friend admitted that she had made up the story because she was upset with the pupil,” Syamsul said.
“Another pupil who knew that the story was untrue also went along with the claim.”
Police subsequently confirmed that the girl had remained inside the school throughout the episode and had not been taken away by any man.
The incident had initially sparked concern at the school before investigators pieced together what had happened.
